name: candidate-count-reproduction-v1
primary_replication: On original-train user-disjoint outer folds, full minus uniform observed top-1 click capture for n>=11. Support requires positive point effects in all three folds and pooled OOF whole-user bootstrap 95% lower bound >0. Not an online CTR claim.
effect_concentration: Separately estimate interaction: (full-uniform for n>=11) minus (full-uniform for 2<=n<=10), resampling the same users across both groups. A larger effect requires its 95% interval lower bound >0; do not infer interaction from one significant subgroup and one nonsignificant subgroup.
secondary: Randomized-display large/small groups, full-ad_only control, top-3, per-seed direction, observed contiguous ranks. These are exploratory intervals without multiplicity adjustment.
reason_diagnostics: In discovery data decompose delta=q*d, where q is any-click request prevalence and d is conditional full-minus-uniform top-1 capture. Symmetric arithmetic decomposition of large-small gap, headroom normalization, user and clicked-product concentration, and label-blind thinning of large requests to 5 candidates. Thinning holds original labels and scores fixed and is not a causal candidate-count intervention.
training: Use original train only for three outer folds. For each outer fold, split other users 80/20 for fit/early stopping by a distinct hash salt. Fit transformer on fit users only; fixed baseline hyperparameters; early stopping on inner LogLoss only. Train full and ad_only at seeds42/43/44. Freeze all 6 models of a fold before scoring its held-out users. Every original-train user is evaluated once. Never read original test.
aggregation: Average per-request outcomes over seeds, not prediction ensemble. Pool OOF rows once per request. Bootstrap conditions on fixed fold models; folds share training users, so do not treat fold scores as independent experiments or estimate full training uncertainty from bootstrap.
limitations: This is resplitting and retraining on a known public development pool, not a fresh external dataset or untouched test. Discovery-validation users never enter replication fitting or evaluation. n>=11 was selected in prior discovery and is now fixed; no threshold search, new feature selection, promotion, bid/revenue simulation or inferred propensity. Non-uniform sampling, historical positions and incomplete candidates remain.
